preamble: Replacement of a glottal stop by the labio-velar glide [w] occurs in several spoken Arabic varieties as Old Arabic hamza (ʔ) was lost. Pattern II verbs with first radical ʔ now begin with w- and inflect like verbs whose first radical is w: ʔaḵḵara 'to delay' appears as waḵḵar in Moroccan and Tunisian (Nefza) Arabic. Outside verbs, Moroccan wudn 'ear' continues ʔuḏn with w- in place of the initial hamza before a rounded vowel. The change affects only some words, analogy with primae-w verbs helps drive it in verbs, and no case outside Arabic has been verified.

examples.note: Pattern II verb with first radical ʔ; the hamza became w, so the verb now inflects as primae w.

examples.to: waxxaṛ – ywaxxaṛ 'to be late; to move backwards'
examples.note: Same development of first-radical ʔ to w in a pattern II verb.

examples.to: وخر waḵḵar 'to step aside, move; to postpone'
examples.note: Same pattern II verb as in Hijazi and Nefza Arabic.
